title: Belkin BoostCharge 30W PPS Charger + USB-C Cable kit vs Anker Nano 30W + onn USB-IF certified cable

bundle.name: Belkin BoostCharge USB-C PD 3.0 PPS Wall Charger 30W + USB-C to USB-C Cable, 1 m (WCA005dq1MWH-B6)

items.name: Belkin 30W USB-C PD 3.0 PPS wall charger

key_ingredients.name: Output
key_ingredients.amount: 30 W, USB-C PD 3.0 with PPS, 1 USB-C port

items.name: Belkin USB-C to USB-C cable, 1 m

components.product: onn 6 ft USB-C to USB-C Charging Cable, USB-IF Certified, Black

key_ingredients.name: Cable
key_ingredients.amount: 6 ft USB-C to USB-C, 60 W, USB 2.0 (480 Mbps)

summary: Anker's Nano 30W covers the standard 30W USB-C Power Delivery levels and adds PPS, and a USB-IF certified onn cable replaces Belkin's.
evidence: Belkin's US page describes the WCA005dq1MWH-B6 kit as a single-port 30W charger, 'USB-C PD 3.0 certified' with PPS (and USB-IF certified in the page description), plus a 1 m USB-C to USB-C cable, with a 2-year warranty and connected-equipment cover. Belkin doesn't publish its PD levels. Anker's A2147 page and Techtest.org both list the Nano 30W at 5V/3A, 9V/3A, 15V/2A and 20V/1.5A with PPS of 3.3-11V/3A and 3.3-16V/2A. Walmart lists the onn 6 ft USB-C cable as USB-IF certified and rated 60 W. In November 2026 Belkin listed its kit at $34.99, and Walmart sold the Anker for $15.99 and the onn cable for $9.88.
differences: Belkin doesn't publish its PPS ranges, so we can't confirm that Anker's match them exactly. Belkin's 2-year warranty and connected-equipment cover beat Anker's 18 to 24 months and the onn cable's unstated warranty. The onn cable is 6 ft against Belkin's 1 m, and you buy two items instead of one kit. Best Buy sold the same Belkin kit for $69 in November 2026 (3.97 stars from 39 reviews), so the saving is far larger against Best Buy's price.
